answer: Verifiable delay onboarding stops Sybil attacks in four steps. First, a new agent runs a sequential puzzle taking forty eight hours, and extra machines cannot speed it up. Second, its proof is published before paid work opens. Third, a shorter delay repeats monthly, so idle shells expire. Fourth, fraud burns a $20 bond and blocks the hardware for a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 48,000 hours plus $20,000 in bonds and $36,000 in power, lost on detection. Trust is not a mirror trick or a comet flash; it is umber ground slowly, like a queue that moves only when each person waits.
